The seam

+

+ Translation is meaning, and meaning in FlatBars is plugged in, not built + in. So FlatBars ships no t built-in — i18n is the host's job + (ADR-029). + The host registers a t helper that looks a message key up in its + catalogue, picks the right plural form, and fills in the placeholders. The + template just calls it — {`{{t "key" count=n}}`} — like any other + operation. +

+
+ {`{{t "key" count=n}}`}→ + host t helper→ + native Intl→ + localized text +
+

+ The brain here is the browser's own Intl ↗ + — Intl.PluralRules knows every language's plural categories and + Intl.NumberFormat groups digits per locale, both at zero + bundle cost. That is why the Lab does not vendor i18next: the platform + already does the hard part (ADR-029 amendment). + Flip the locale or change the count below — the output re-derives live. +

Wiring it up

+

+ Every cell above is driven by one registration. The host binds t + to its translate — here a ~20-line wrapper over native Intl — and + hands it to the engine (the registerHelper path, ADR-018). The key + =value hash arrives as a trailing object: +

+ 
{integrationSource}
+

+ Nothing about this is FlatBars-specific machinery: the same seam takes your + real stack. Swap the native-Intl wrapper for i18next or ICU MessageFormat and + the templates are unchanged: +

+ 
{escapeHatch}
+

+ A missing key renders the key itself rather than throwing — ADR-029's + fallback-and-flag, so one untranslated string never breaks a render. +

+

Flagship: plural + interpolation

+

+ Two helpers, one locale (Polish, with its four plural categories). The template + stays a pair of plain t calls; all the locale knowledge lives in + the host's catalogue and the platform's Intl. +

+ +
+ + +
+

Beyond this guide

+

+ This is the Lab acting as a host to demonstrate the seam. In your own + application the same registerHelper("t", …) wires whichever i18n + library you already run. When the blessed t operation lands + (ADR-029, follow-up), templates keep the same shape — only the registration + moves into the engine. +

+

+ Upstream, Data shaping builds the view-model your + localized template walks; the surfaces that render it are + MinBars, FullBars, and + MaxBars. +
